chunks: Abu Qays narrated to me from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام, who said:
The salat on the day of ʿEid is only upon the one who goes out to the open prayer ground, and whoever does not go out, then there is no salat upon him.

So this does not contradict what we have mentioned earlier, because the meaning of his saying عليه السلام, 'there is no salat upon him,' is: not as an obligation, as it is when one goes out to the open prayer ground; and likewise.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the ritual prayer, here referring to the ʿEid salat
key_terms.الْجَبَّانَةِ: the open prayer ground outside the town
key_terms.فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ صَلَاةٌ: there is no prayer binding upon him, meaning no obligation in this context
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْعِيدِ: the day of the ʿEid festival

ai.seo_question: When does the ʿEid salat become obligatory according to this hadith from al-Istibṣār?
ai.summary: This narration states that the ʿEid salat is incumbent upon the one who goes out to the prayer ground. It further clarifies that for one who does not go out, the prayer is not obligatory in the same way, which aligns with the chapter's legal discussion about the conditions of obligation.
